history.rationale: Initial baseline with moderate depth, conservative learning rate, and mild regularization to establish a benchmark for imbalanced overtake prediction.
Trial 1 got 0.345 with depth 4; testing shallower depth 3 with higher min_child_weight=5 to see if reducing tree complexity curbs false positives.
Trial 2 improved to 0.379 with depth 3, so testing depth 2 with slightly more trees to test whether an even simpler model prevents overfitting further.
Depth 3 outperformed depth 2 and 4, so testing depth 5 with lower learning rate and stronger L1/L2 regularization to check if deeper interactions help without overfitting.
Trial 4 reached 0.386 with depth 5 and high regularization; testing depth 6 with slightly higher min_child_weight=8 to explore deeper trees with strong constraints.
Trial 5 reached 0.391 at depth 6; testing depth 7 with min_child_weight=9 and higher regularization to test the depth limit.
Trial 5 found depth 6 optimal (0.391); testing a lower learning rate 0.02 with 300 estimators to see if finer shrinkage improves convergence.
Trial 7 achieved 0.3987 with lr 0.02 and 300 trees; testing lr 0.015 with 400 trees to explore if slower shrinkage continues to yield gains.
Trial 7 was best with min_child_weight=8; testing min_child_weight=7 to see if slightly more leaf granularity helps at lr=0.02.
Trial 9 showed lower PR-AUC with min_child_weight=7 compared to 8; testing min_child_weight=9 to see if higher regularization of leaf size improves performance.
Trial 7 set colsample_bytree=0.6; testing colsample_bytree=0.5 to evaluate whether greater feature subsampling reduces inter-tree correlation.
Trial 11 showed 0.5 colsample degraded performance; testing colsample_bytree=0.7 to see if more feature coverage improves over 0.6.
Trial 7 used subsample=0.75; testing higher subsample=0.85 to check if preserving more training instances per tree improves positive class representation.
Subsample=0.85 decreased PR-AUC to 0.3929; testing subsample=0.70 to check if slightly lower instance sampling performs better than 0.75.
With 0.75 (0.3987) outperforming 0.70 (0.3930) and 0.85 (0.3929), testing intermediate subsample=0.80 to fine-tune instance sampling.
Trial 7 achieved best PR-AUC with reg_lambda=5.0; testing stronger L2 regularization reg_lambda=7.0 to see if it reduces variance further.
reg_lambda=7 gave 0.3984 and 5 gave 0.3987; testing reg_lambda=4.0 to see if slightly less L2 regularization improves score.
Both reg_lambda=5.0 (0.3987) and 7.0 (0.3984) beat 4.0 (0.3932); testing reg_lambda=6.0 to see if the peak lies in between.
Trial 7 had reg_alpha=0.3; testing higher L1 regularization reg_alpha=0.5 to induce sparser feature selection in deep trees.
reg_alpha=0.5 decreased performance to 0.395; testing reg_alpha=0.2 to check if slightly less L1 sparsity than 0.3 improves the score.
Trial 7 best at colsample 0.60 (0.3987) over 0.70 (0.3935); testing 0.65 to see if an intermediate feature fraction beats 0.60.
Trial 21 confirmed 0.65 is worse than 0.60; testing 0.55 between 0.50 and 0.60 to pinpoint the optimal colsample_bytree.
Trial 7 achieved peak score at 300 estimators; testing 250 estimators to see if 300 overshot slightly.
Trial 23 improved to 0.4009 at 250 estimators; testing 220 estimators to check if an even earlier stopping point performs better.
250 estimators gave 0.4009 and 220 gave 0.3998; testing 260 estimators to locate the optimum between 250 and 300.
Trial 25 reached 0.4015 at 260 estimators; testing 270 estimators to see if the peak is slightly higher.
Testing slightly higher learning rate 0.022 with proportionally fewer trees (240) to see if early convergence yields better generalization.
Trial 27 set a new best of 0.4042 with lr=0.022 and 240 trees; testing 230 trees to fine-tune the tree count.
With 230 giving 0.4036 and 240 giving 0.4042, testing 250 trees at lr=0.022 to see if slightly more boosting rounds improves PR-AUC further.
Trial 27 peaked at lr=0.022/240; testing lr=0.023 with 235 trees to see if slight shrinkage acceleration peaks even higher.
